requirements.title: Start a ready item and accept its implementer session
requirements.rationale: An approved plan should turn into a pushed version without the person, and a session's own account of its work is not evidence.

criteria.condition: a `ready` item's package names, in the `dependencies` of its `tasks.json`, a package that is not finished at the tip of the workspace's default branch: the directory with that number under `.specs/` there does not exist, does not load with `afspec.LoadSpec`, or `IsFinished` is false for it
criteria.action: refuse the item in the start guard `dependency`, registered with `Scheduler.RegisterGuard`, with the reason `package <NN> on <default branch>` naming the first such dependency in the plan's order; read the default branch from the hub (`GET …/scm/tree` of `.specs` and `GET …/scm/file` of the package's files at the workspace's `head_sha`) at most once in 30 seconds per workspace, an injected interval; and allow an item that is not `ready`, whose package names no dependency, or whose dependencies are all finished
criteria.contract: the guard returns `(false, "package 03 on main", nil)` while the dependency is unfinished and `(true, "", nil)` at the first read after it is finished; an item that touches the same files as another is allowed; a hub error is returned as the guard's error, which the scheduler treats as a refusal

setup: a fake hub (internal/hubtest) whose workspace `demo` serves `scm/tree` and `scm/file` from a repository fixture built with afspec
an item 7 in `ready` whose package names the dependencies of the row
an injected clock
check.pseudocode: new file internal/impl/guard_test.go, a table over the default branch's .specs on the fake hub {03 with a pending task -> (false, 'package 03 on main'); 03 with every task done -> (true, ''); 03 sealed -> (true, ''); no directory 03_* -> (false, 'package 03 on main'); 03 whose tasks.json is not JSON -> (false, 'package 03 on main'); dependencies [02 done, 03 pending, 04 pending] -> names 03; no dependencies -> (true, ''); item in 'implementing' -> (true, '') without a hub request; hub stopped -> err != nil}: ok, reason, err = svc.DependencyGuard(ctx, item); assert as the row says. Then: advance the clock 10s and ask again -> the fake hub saw no further request; advance 30s -> it saw one

criteria.condition: the scheduler calls the step of an item in `ready`
criteria.action: create the item's task fork with package 05's `change.Service.EnsureFork` where the item has none; set the item's change to open with `PATCH …/changes/{number}` `{"state":"open"}` where it is a draft; read the change's current version number, 0 for an item without a change; and, while the item is still `ready`, ask the scheduler for an implementer session with `session.Spec{Item, Role: implementer, Step: "implement", Fork, Branch, Prompt, Accept}`, the prompt being `/af-impl <package directory> --unattended --no-merge --result {result}`
criteria.contract: the hub's change is `open` before the session is asked for; an item whose change is open already sends no `PATCH`; an imported package's item gets a fork and no change; the package directory is `source.dir` for an item of kind `spec` and `Dir` of package 05's `plan.Service.Kept` otherwise; when `RunSession` returns `sched.ErrNotStarted`, or a result whose outcome is not `completed`, the step returns nil and leaves the item's state as it is

the impl service over the real item service, inbox, store and package 05's change service, a stub of its `plan.Service.Kept`, and a stub scheduler whose RunSession the test scripts and whose requests, RecordFailure and OpenSessionFailed calls it records
check.pseudocode: new file internal/impl/start_test.go, a table over {planned item with a draft change 4 -> the fake hub saw PATCH changes/4 {state: open} before the request and no fork request; planned item whose change is open -> no PATCH; item of kind spec without a fork -> one fork created through EnsureFork, no change request; RunSession scripted to return sched.ErrNotStarted -> step returns nil and state == 'ready'; outcome 'failed' -> nil and state unchanged}: err = svc.Step(ctx, item); assert the recorded request == {Item, Role: 'implementer', Step: 'implement', Fork: rec.Fork, Branch: rec.Branch, Prompt: '/af-impl .specs/12_greeting --unattended --no-merge --result {result}'} and that its Accept is set

criteria.condition: the event `session.started` is appended to the event log for an implementer session of an item that is `ready`
criteria.action: move the item to `implementing` through the item service's `Transition`, with the reason `implementer session started`
criteria.contract: the item's state is `implementing` and its thread has the entry `ready -> implementing: implementer session started`; a `session.started` of a planner or a reviewer, or of an item in another state, moves nothing and logs no error

check.pseudocode: in internal/impl/start_test.go, with the service following a real event log: a table over {implementer session of a ready item -> eventually state == 'implementing'; reviewer session of a ready item -> state stays 'ready'; implementer session of an item in 'implementing' -> unchanged, one `state` entry in all}: log.Append('session.started', {session, item, role}); assert as the row says

criteria.condition: an implementer session asked with `--no-merge` has ended, the item's change on the hub has a version greater than at the session's start, and the package read from the hub at that version's head (`GET …/scm/file` of its `prd.md`, `requirements.json`, `tasks.json` and `progress.json`, loaded with `afspec.LoadSpec`) has no task `pending` or `in_progress`
criteria.action: accept the session by returning nil from the accept function, having first, for an item that had no change and whose branch is on the fork, opened the change through package 05's `change.Service.OpenDraft` with the item's title, the text of the package's `## Intent` section and the session's id, and set it open
criteria.contract: the session's outcome is `completed` whatever `outcome` its result file names; an imported package's item has an open change at version 1 afterwards; the step goes on to the evaluation of that version in the same call

criteria.condition: an implementer session has ended and the item's change has no version greater than at the session's start (or the item has no change and its branch is not on the fork), or the package at the new version's head has a task `pending` or `in_progress`, or the package cannot be read from the hub or does not load
criteria.action: refuse the session by returning an error from the accept function, create no item from its result file, evaluate nothing and run no gate
criteria.contract: the accept function's error is `no new version`, `tasks still open` or `package does not load: <first line of the error>`, which package 04 records as the failed session's reason; the item's state and its stored findings are unchanged; a session that left no result file is failed by package 04 with `no result` and the accept function is not called

criteria.condition: an accepted implementer session's result file lists `open_items`
criteria.action: create for each entry, in the file's order, a work item with the item service's `CreateLinked(ctx, item, "defect", text)`, the text being the entry's `title`, then `missing`, `why` and `closes: <closes>` where they are present, each as a paragraph of its own, cut to 20,000 code points; and skip an entry whose title is the title of an item already linked to this parent
criteria.contract: each new item is of kind `defect`, in `new`, with `parent` set, and the parent's thread has one `linked_item` entry for each; no session is asked for a new item; handling the same result file twice creates each item once; a result file without `open_items`, or with an empty list, creates none

in internal/impl/start_test.go: result = {outcome: 'complete_with_open_items', open_items: [{kind: 'defect', title: 'Log line missing', missing: 'm', why: 'w', closes: 'c'}, {kind: 'awaits', title: 'Waits for 09'}]}; svc.HandleResult(ctx, item, result); kids = items.Get(item).Children; assert len(kids) == 2; assert each has kind 'defect', state 'new'; assert the first's text == 'Log line missing

m

w

closes: c' and the second's == 'Waits for 09'; assert the parent's thread has two linked_item entries; assert the stub scheduler saw no request for a child; svc.HandleResult again -> still 2 children; a result without open_items -> no child

requirements.title: Send work back to the implementer as findings
requirements.rationale: A failed gate, an objection, a comment, a conflict and a failed health command all mean the same thing to the implementer: change the finished work, and say what was done about each point.

criteria.condition: a part of nightshift calls `(*impl.Service).Rework(ctx, item, findings)` with at least one finding, each with a `Text` that is not empty and a `Source` of `gate`, `review`, `person`, `health` or `conflict`, for an item in `ready`, `implementing`, `reviewing` or `landing`
criteria.action: store the findings in the given order after those already waiting for the item, giving each finding without an `ID` the next id `f<n>` of the item and setting `Binding` on every finding of the source `person`; move an item that is `reviewing` or `landing` to `implementing` with the reason `rework: <n> findings (<sources>)`; and wake the scheduler
criteria.contract: returns nil; the findings are still waiting after a restart of the daemon; an item in `ready` or `implementing` keeps its state; a finding whose `ID` is already stored for the item is stored once, so a caller that is called twice may call twice

check.pseudocode: new file internal/impl/rework_test.go, a table over the item's state {ready, implementing, reviewing, landing}: err = svc.Rework(ctx, n, [{Source: 'review', Text: 'a', File: 'x.go', Line: 3}, {Source: 'person', Text: 'b'}]); assert err == nil; w = svc.Waiting(n); assert ids == ['f1','f2'] and w[1].Binding and not w[0].Binding; assert state == 'implementing' except for ready, which stays; for reviewing assert the thread's last entry == 'reviewing -> implementing: rework: 2 findings (review, person)'; assert the scheduler was woken. Then: Rework(n, [{ID: 'blocked-5', Source: 'person', Text: 'c'}]) twice -> one finding 'blocked-5', after f1 and f2; reopen the store -> svc.Waiting(n) is the same three

criteria.condition: `Rework` is called with no finding, with a finding whose `Text` is empty or whose `Source` is none of the five, for an item nightshift does not know, or for an item in `new`, `planning`, `awaiting_approval`, `verifying`, `publishing`, `done` or `abandoned`
criteria.action: refuse the call, store no finding and leave the item's state as it is
criteria.contract: the error satisfies `errors.Is` with `impl.ErrInvalid` for the findings, with the item service's `ErrNotFound` for the item and with `impl.ErrState` for the state; the count of stored findings and of thread entries is unchanged

check.pseudocode: in internal/impl/rework_test.go, a table over {findings nil -> ErrInvalid; [{Source: 'review', Text: ''}] -> ErrInvalid; [{Source: 'robot', Text: 'x'}] -> ErrInvalid; one good and one bad finding -> ErrInvalid and none stored; item 999 -> item.ErrNotFound; an item in each of the seven states -> ErrState}: err = svc.Rework(ctx, n, f); assert errors.Is(err, want); assert len(svc.Waiting(n)) and the thread's entry count unchanged

criteria.condition: the step of an `implementing` item runs, findings wait for the item, and the package at the head of the change's current version has no task `pending` or `in_progress`
criteria.action: ask the scheduler for an implementer session with the step `implement`, the prompt `/af-impl <package directory> --unattended --rework {input:findings} --result {result}` and the input `findings`: one JSON array of the waiting findings in their order, each an object with `id`, `source`, `text` and, where they are set, `file`, `line`, `criterion`, `output` and `binding`
criteria.contract: the input parses as an array whose ids are those waiting, in order; a finding of the source `person` carries `"binding": true`; a member that is not set is absent, not empty; while the package has an open task the request is the `--no-merge` one of a first implementation and the findings stay waiting

Second case: task 2 of the package pending at the head -> req.Prompt holds '--no-merge' and no Inputs, and svc.Waiting(n) still has both

criteria.condition: a rework session has ended with a result file that lists `replies`
criteria.action: append to the item's thread, for each reply in the file's order, one entry of the kind `reply` with the text `<finding id> <action>: <text>`, cut to 2,000 characters and not marking the thread unread, and store the reply with the finding it names, whether or not the session is accepted afterwards
criteria.contract: the thread has one `reply` entry per reply, in order, before the session's `session_ended` entry; the stored finding carries the reply's `action` and `text`; a reply that names no finding given to the session is written to the thread and stored with none

check.pseudocode: in internal/impl/rework_test.go: two findings f1, f2 waiting; RunSession scripted to call Accept with {outcome: 'nothing_changed', replies: [{id: 'f1', action: 'declined', text: 'the test already covers it'}, {id: 'f2', action: 'not_reproduced', text: 'passes'}, {id: 'zz', action: 'fixed', text: 'x'}]} and no push; svc.Step(ctx, n); assert the thread's last three entries of kind 'reply' == ['f1 declined: the test already covers it', 'f2 not_reproduced: passes', 'zz fixed: x'] and the thread is not unread; assert svc.History(n) holds f1 with the reply declined; assert Accept returned an error (the session is not accepted)

criteria.condition: a rework session has ended and the item's change on the hub has a version greater than at the session's start
criteria.action: accept the session by returning nil from the accept function, take the findings that were given to it out of those waiting and keep them with their replies as the item's history, create the linked items of its `open_items` as for a first implementation, and go on to the evaluation of the new version
criteria.contract: the session's outcome is `completed`; no finding given to it waits any longer; a finding stored while the session ran still waits and starts the next rework; the new version has no gate verdict and no review verdict

the impl service over the real item service, inbox, store and package 05's change service, a stub of its `plan.Service.Kept`, and a stub scheduler whose RunSession the test scripts and whose requests, RecordFailure and OpenSessionFailed calls it records

criteria.condition: a rework session has ended and the item's change has no version greater than at the session's start
criteria.action: refuse the session by returning an error from the accept function and keep every finding that was given to it waiting
criteria.contract: the accept function's error is `no new version`, which package 04 records as the failed session's reason, for a result file whose outcome is `nothing_changed`, `rework_failed` or `push_failed` alike; the next rework session is given the same findings; the item's state is unchanged

check.pseudocode: in internal/impl/rework_test.go, a table over the result's outcome {nothing_changed, rework_failed, push_failed, reworked without a push}: f1 waiting; RunSession calls Accept with that result and pushes nothing; assert Accept's error == 'no new version'; assert ids(svc.Waiting(n)) == ['f1']; svc.Step(ctx, n) again -> the second request's findings input holds f1

criteria.condition: the scheduler calls the step of an item in `implementing`
criteria.action: do the first of these that applies, and then the next, until a session ended otherwise than `completed`, a decision of the item is open, an error occurred or the item has left `implementing`: restore the item's fork when the hub no longer has it; send a check report the hub has not taken and do what follows its verdict; start the implementer with `--no-merge` when the item has no change or the package at the change's head has an open task; start a rework when findings wait; evaluate the change's current version when it is not evaluated; run the gate when the version has no gate verdict; move the item to `reviewing` when the gate passed on the current version
criteria.contract: what the step does depends only on the hub's change, the package at its head and what the store holds for the item, so a step called after a restart, a resume or a version a person pushed does what a first call would; a version whose gate failed and for which a finding waits starts a rework, not a second gate

check.pseudocode: new file internal/impl/step_test.go, a table over the item's facts -> the first thing the step does (each of session, evaluation and gate replaced by a recording stub): {no change -> no-merge session; change at version 1, task pending at its head -> no-merge session; tasks done, finding waiting -> rework session; tasks done, findings waiting and a task pending -> no-merge session; tasks done, version 2 not evaluated -> evaluation of 2; version 2 evaluated, no gate verdict -> gate on 2; gate passed on 2 but version 3 is current (pushed by a person) -> evaluation of 3; gate verdict stored for 2, report not taken, a finding waiting -> the report first, then the rework, no gate; gate passed on current version -> Transition to 'reviewing'; open decision on the item -> nothing}: svc.Step(ctx, n); assert the first recorded action

criteria.condition: a later package has set a class for an item with `(*impl.Service).SetClass(ctx, item, class)`
criteria.action: ask for every implementer and reviewer session of that item with that class
criteria.contract: the `Class` of each `sched.Request` for the item is the class set, `sched.ClassRepair` for a repair; an item with no class set is asked for with the zero class, so that the scheduler places it by its state; the class survives a restart

check.pseudocode: in internal/impl/step_test.go: svc.SetClass(ctx, n, sched.ClassRepair); svc.Rework(n, one finding); svc.Step(ctx, n); assert the recorded request's Class == sched.ClassRepair; reopen the store and step again -> the same; an item m without SetClass -> Class == the zero value

requirements.title: Evaluate and gate every version
requirements.rationale: A version that can never land should cost nothing more, and one that can has to pass the package's own checks on a clone the session did not prepare.

criteria.condition: nightshift reads the hub's evaluation of a version it has not evaluated (`GET …/changes/{number}` with `include=overlaps`) and a requirement of its `landing` has `block` true
criteria.action: open a decision of the kind `blocked` on the item's thread, with the question `Version <v> of item <N> touches paths that rule <rule> blocks. Revise it or abandon the item?`, as evidence the change's URL and, for each blocking requirement, the rule's name with the files that selected it, `revise` recommended and `item <N>` as what it blocks; record the version as evaluated; and run no gate on it
criteria.contract: the kind `blocked` is declared in the inbox's registry with exactly the options `revise`, which requires a comment, and `abandon`; one decision is open per version however often the step runs; the item keeps its state and its `waiting_on` names the decision; the hub received no check report for that version

setup: a fake hub (internal/hubtest) holding the workspace `demo`, its forks, changes with versions, checks and a policy

the impl service over the real item service, inbox, store and package 05's change service, a stub of its `plan.Service.Kept`, and a stub scheduler whose RunSession the test scripts and whose requests, RecordFailure and OpenSessionFailed calls it records
check.pseudocode: new file internal/impl/evaluate_test.go: the fake hub's policy blocks 'secrets/**'; version 2 of the item's change touches secrets/key.pem and api/greet.go; svc.Step(ctx, n) twice; d = the item's open decisions; assert len(d) == 1 and d[0].Kind == 'blocked'; assert option keys == ['revise','abandon'] with comment_required only on revise and revise recommended; assert the question == 'Version 2 of item 12 touches paths that rule nightshift-1 blocks. Revise it or abandon the item?'; assert the evidence names 'nightshift-1' and 'secrets/key.pem' and not 'api/greet.go'; assert items.Get(n).State == 'implementing' and its waiting_on.kind == 'blocked'; assert fakeHub.Checks(change) is empty and the gate stub was not called

criteria.condition: a `blocked` decision is answered
criteria.action: carry the answer out in the handler registered with the inbox's `OnAnswer`: for `revise`, call `Rework` with one finding of the source `person`, the id `blocked-<decision id>` and the comment as its text; for `abandon`, call the item service's `Abandon` with the reason `blocked: abandoned by the person`
criteria.contract: after `revise` the item is `implementing`, also when the decision was opened for an item in `landing`, and one binding finding with the comment waits, however often the handler is called; after `abandon` the item is `abandoned`

check.pseudocode: in internal/impl/evaluate_test.go, a table over {state implementing, revise 'drop the key file' -> one waiting finding {ID: 'blocked-<id>', Source: 'person', Binding: true, Text: 'drop the key file'}, state 'implementing'; state landing (decision opened with svc.OpenBlocked), revise -> the same and state 'implementing'; abandon -> state 'abandoned' and the thread names the reason}: inbox.Answer(d.ID, option, comment); eventually assert as the row says; call the handler a second time directly -> still one finding

criteria.condition: an item is paused (`Scheduler.Paused`) and a decision of the kind `blocked` or `review_disagreement` of it is answered
criteria.action: store the answer and carry it out when the item is resumed, through a function registered with `Scheduler.OnResume`, in the order of the answers; both kinds register their handlers through `(*impl.Service).OnAnswer(kind, option, fn)`, which does this
criteria.contract: the handler returns nil at once; until the resume the item's state, its waiting findings and the hub's checks are unchanged; after the resume the effect is the one the answer has for an item that is not paused

check.pseudocode: in internal/impl/evaluate_test.go, with the stub scheduler's Paused(n) == true, a table over {blocked/revise, blocked/abandon, two answers to two decisions of a kind the test registers through svc.OnAnswer with a recording handler}: answer the decision; assert the handler returned nil; assert state and len(svc.Waiting(n)) unchanged and the recording handler not called; set Paused false and call the registered OnResume function with n; assert the effect of the row (a waiting binding finding; state 'abandoned'; the recording handler saw both answers in their order)

criteria.condition: nightshift evaluates a version of which no requirement blocks
criteria.action: take the files of the change's `paths` that are outside the plan (a file is inside when an entry of a task's `touches` equals its path or names a directory above it, or when it lies in the package's own directory), store that list for the item, and, when it is not empty and differs from the list last written for the item, append to the thread one entry of the kind `outside_plan` with the text `outside the plan: <files>`: the first 50 in path order, joined with `, `, followed by ` and <n> more` when there are more
criteria.contract: `(*impl.Service).OutsidePlan(ctx, item)` returns the whole list; a version whose files are all inside the plan writes no entry; a later version with the same list writes none; the gate runs on the version whatever the list holds

check.pseudocode: in internal/impl/evaluate_test.go, the package's tasks touching ['api/greet.go', 'internal/greet', 'docs/'], a table over the version's paths {['api/greet.go', 'internal/greet/a.go', 'docs/api.md', '.specs/12_greeting/progress.json'] -> no entry, OutsidePlan == []; those plus ['README.md', 'api/other.go'] -> entry 'outside the plan: README.md, api/other.go'; 'internal/greeting/x.go' -> outside (a name that only starts like a touched directory); 60 files outside -> the first 50 and ' and 10 more', OutsidePlan has 60; the next version with the same two files -> no second entry; then one file more -> a new entry}: svc.Evaluate(ctx, n); assert the thread's outside_plan entries and svc.OutsidePlan(n); assert the gate stub was called for every row

criteria.condition: the current version of an `implementing` item is evaluated without a block, has no gate verdict, and `speca`'s gate answers `pass` for it
criteria.action: bring the clone `<sessions.dir>/items/<N>/gate` to the version's head with `gitclone.Sync` from the fork's git URL and the worker token; run in it, through `command.Runner` and so as the session user, `speca <package directory> --gate full --timeout <gate.timeout>` with `XDG_STATE_HOME` naming an empty directory made for this run and removed after it; store the verdict; report the check `nightshift-gate` as `passed` on that version with `speca`'s `summary`; append to the thread an entry of the kind `check` with the text `nightshift-gate passed on version <v>: <summary>`; set the item's count of failed gates in a row to zero; and move the item to `reviewing`
criteria.contract: the hub holds `nightshift-gate` with `status` `passed`, that `version` and a `summary` of at most 2,000 characters; the command ran with the clone at the version's head as its working directory; the item is `reviewing`; a later step for the same version runs no gate

symbols.name: GET …/changes/{number}
symbols.signature: scope changes:read (satisfied by changes:write); query include=versions,overlaps,approvals,checks; 200 change object {number, ref, title, intent, state: draft|open|landed|abandoned, source: {workspace_slug, branch}, version: int, head_sha, base_sha, paths: [string] (at most 2,000), paths_truncated, landing: {status: ready|pending|blocked, reason, requirements: [{rule, paths (first 50), approvals: {required, counted, approvers}, checks: [{name, status}], block: bool, satisfied: bool}]}, versions?: [{number, head_sha, base_sha, kind, created_at}], overlaps?: [overlap entry]}

symbols.name: PATCH …/changes/{number}
symbols.signature: scope changes:write; body {"state": "open"} marks a draft ready (the intent rule must hold), {"state": "draft"} turns it back; 200 with the change object

symbols.name: PUT …/changes/{number}/checks/{name}
symbols.signature: scope checks:write; a token bound to a task fork gets 403 token_bound; body {status: pending|passed|failed (required), version: int, summary: string of at most 2,000 characters, url?, details?}; one result per version and name, a report replaces the earlier one whole; 200 with the check

symbols.name: GET …/changes/{number}/diff
symbols.signature: scope changes:read; query version=<n>|latest, format=json|patch, patches=true|false; without `against` the diff from the version's base_sha to its head_sha; format=patch answers text/x-diff, cut at 8 MiB with the header X-Parley-Truncated: true; 404 not_found for a version the change does not have, 404 ref_not_found when its commits are gone

symbols.name: GET …/changes/{number}/overlaps
symbols.signature: one overlap entry per other draft or open change with the same target branch and a file in common: {change: {number, ref, title, state, version, …}, paths (first 100), paths_truncated, count}; empty for a landed or abandoned change; 404 change_not_found; the same entries as the member `overlaps` of GET …/changes/{number}?include=overlaps

symbols.name: version ref
symbols.signature: the head of each version, kept in the target workspace's repository also for a fork source and after the fork is gone; a task fork reads its parent's objects

symbols.name: PATCH /api/v1/workspaces/{slug}
symbols.signature: for a task fork, body {"ttl": "7d"} (a whole number and m, h or d, from 5m to [forks].max_ttl) sets expires_at to now plus ttl; 400 invalid_request on a repository workspace; 200 with the workspace object

symbols.name: GET …/scm/file
symbols.signature: scope git:read (satisfied by git:write); query path (required), ref (a revision; default the default branch); 200 the file's bytes as application/octet-stream; 404 path_not_found

symbols.name: POST …/scm/refs
symbols.signature: scope git:write; body {name: <branch>, sha: <full commit id>}; 201 with the ref object; 404 ref_not_found, 409 ref_exists

symbols.name: POST …/scm/commits
symbols.signature: scope git:write; body {branch, base_ref (required when the branch does not exist), message, operations: [{op: "put", path, content | content_base64}]}; makes one commit and creates or moves the branch

symbols.name: POST …/changes
symbols.signature: refuses with 400 nothing_to_land a source branch that has no commit the target lacks, and with 409 change_exists a branch that is the source of a draft or open change (called through package 05)
